name: COBOL
title: COBOL: records, money and plain English
intro: COBOL (COmmon Business-Oriented Language) was designed in 1959 for business data: names, amounts, dates and records. It is still in daily use at banks, insurers and government agencies, where it runs payroll, payments and benefits on mainframes, and those systems need people who can read and maintain it. COBOL reads like stiff English: ADD TAX TO TOTAL. These lessons use free format, which modern compilers accept; older code puts each part of a line in fixed columns, and lesson 1 shows how. Every example is a whole program and shows exactly what it prints. To run one yourself with GnuCOBOL, save it as hello.cob and type cobc -x -free hello.cob && ./hello.

sections.p: A COBOL program is split into divisions. The IDENTIFICATION DIVISION names the program. The PROCEDURE DIVISION holds the statements that run, top to bottom. DISPLAY prints a line, and STOP RUN ends the program. Sentences end with a full stop.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. HELLO.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY "Hello, squirrel!".
    DISPLAY "Nuts are ready.".
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: DISPLAY prints every item you give it, one after the other with nothing in between, and then ends the line. *> starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. JOIN.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    *> Two items, no space added between them
    DISPLAY "Acorn" "Bank".
    DISPLAY "Acorn " "Bank".
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: Code written for older compilers uses a fixed layout from the days of punched cards. Columns 1 to 6 hold a sequence number, column 7 marks a comment with *, division and paragraph names start in column 8 (area A), and statements start in column 12 or later (area B). Anything past column 72 is ignored. You will meet this layout in nearly every existing system, so it is worth recognising, even though the lessons here use free format.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY "Pay" "day".
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: DISPLAY puts the items right next to each other. Add a space inside one of the strings if you want one.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY "One".
    *> DISPLAY "Two".
    DISPLAY "Three".
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: The middle line is a comment, so it never runs. Each DISPLAY ends its own line.

practice.q: Which division holds the statements that run?
practice.why: The IDENTIFICATION DIVISION names the program, the DATA DIVISION describes data, and the PROCEDURE DIVISION is the code.

practice.q: Where is COBOL still widely used today?
practice.why: Much of the world's payment, payroll and benefits processing still runs on COBOL.

practice.q: In fixed-format code, what does a * in column 7 mean?
practice.why: Column 7 is the indicator area. * marks a comment line, and - marks a continued line.

lessons.title: Data and pictures
lessons.summary: WORKING-STORAGE, PIC 9 and PIC X, MOVE.

sections.p: Every variable is declared up front in the DATA DIVISION, under WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. A picture (PIC) says exactly what the field holds. 9 is one digit and X is one character, and a number in brackets repeats it: PIC 9(3) is three digits, PIC X(8) is eight characters. 01 is the level number of a stand-alone item.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PICS.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 NUTS PIC 9(3) VALUE 42.
01 OWNER PIC X(8) VALUE "Squirrel".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY OWNER " has " NUTS " nuts".
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: A field always shows its full width. A three-digit number prints with leading zeros, and a short text value is padded with spaces on the right. A value that is too long is cut off: text loses its right end, and a number loses its leftmost digits.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. SIZES.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 CODE-A PIC X(4).
01 AMOUNT PIC 9(2).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE "AB" TO CODE-A.
    DISPLAY "[" CODE-A "]".
    MOVE "OAKTREE" TO CODE-A.
    DISPLAY "[" CODE-A "]".
    MOVE 1234 TO AMOUNT.
    DISPLAY AMOUNT.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: An edited picture formats a number for people. Z is a digit that shows as a space when it is a leading zero. Move a plain number into an edited field to print it neatly.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. EDITED.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 NUTS PIC 9(4) VALUE 42.
01 NUTS-OUT PIC ZZZ9.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE NUTS TO NUTS-OUT.
    DISPLAY "[" NUTS "]".
    DISPLAY "[" NUTS-OUT "]".
    STOP RUN.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(3) VALUE 7.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: PIC 9(3) is always three digits wide, so 7 shows with two leading zeros.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 T PIC X(3).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE "PINECONE" TO T.
    DISPLAY T.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: Text is cut off on the right when it does not fit, so only the first three characters stay.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q3.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(2).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE 365 TO N.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: A number that is too big loses its leftmost digits. This silent truncation is a classic COBOL bug, so size fields generously.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q4.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(3) VALUE 5.
01 E PIC ZZ9.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE N TO E.
    DISPLAY "[" E "]".
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: Each Z turns a leading zero into a space. The final 9 always shows a digit.
X is one character of any kind, and (10) repeats it ten times.

lessons.title: Arithmetic
lessons.summary: ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, COMPUTE and decimals.

sections.p: COBOL has an English verb for each operation. ADD A TO B changes B. With GIVING, the result goes into a separate field and the inputs are left alone.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VERBS.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 TOTAL PIC 9(3) VALUE 10.
01 RESULT PIC 9(3).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    ADD 5 TO TOTAL.
    DISPLAY TOTAL.
    SUBTRACT 3 FROM TOTAL.
    DISPLAY TOTAL.
    MULTIPLY TOTAL BY 2 GIVING RESULT.
    DISPLAY RESULT.
    DIVIDE RESULT BY 4 GIVING RESULT.
    DISPLAY RESULT.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: COMPUTE takes an ordinary formula with + - * / and brackets. Whole-number fields drop any fraction, they do not round it. DIVIDE ... REMAINDER gives you what is left over.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. COMP.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 Q PIC 9(3).
01 R PIC 9(3).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    COMPUTE Q = (2 + 3) * 4.
    DISPLAY Q.
    DIVIDE 17 BY 5 GIVING Q REMAINDER R.
    DISPLAY Q " remainder " R.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: V in a picture marks where the decimal point is assumed to be. PIC 9(3)V99 holds amounts like 123.45 exactly, without the rounding errors of floating point, which is why banks like it. To print the point, move the value into an edited picture with a real . in it. ROUNDED rounds instead of cutting off.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. MONEY.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 PRICE PIC 9(3)V99 VALUE 19.99.
01 TOTAL PIC 9(4)V99.
01 SHARE PIC 9(3)V99.
01 SHOW PIC ZZZ9.99.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MULTIPLY PRICE BY 3 GIVING TOTAL.
    MOVE TOTAL TO SHOW.
    DISPLAY "Total:" SHOW.
    COMPUTE SHARE ROUNDED = 10 / 3.
    MOVE SHARE TO SHOW.
    DISPLAY "Share:" SHOW.
    STOP RUN.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(2) VALUE 8.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    ADD 4 TO N.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: ADD 4 TO N adds 4 to N and stores the result back in N.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(2).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DIVIDE 9 BY 2 GIVING N.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: N has no decimal places, so the .5 is dropped. Without ROUNDED, COBOL cuts off, it does not round.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q3.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(2).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DIVIDE 9 BY 2 GIVING N ROUNDED.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: ROUNDED rounds 4.5 up to 5.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q4.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 Q PIC 9.
01 R PIC 9.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DIVIDE 7 BY 3 GIVING Q REMAINDER R.
    DISPLAY Q R.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: 7 is 3 twice with 1 left over, so Q is 2 and R is 1, printed side by side.

practice.q: Why is PIC 9(5)V99 good for money?
options: It stores the cents exactly, with no floating-point rounding
It makes numbers print in colour
practice.answer: It stores the cents exactly, with no floating-point rounding
practice.why: V marks an assumed decimal point and the digits are stored exactly, so 0.10 + 0.20 is exactly 0.30.

lessons.title: Decisions
lessons.summary: IF, EVALUATE and level-88 condition names.

sections.p: IF runs statements when a condition is true, ELSE when it is not, and END-IF closes it. Conditions can be written with symbols (> < =) or words (GREATER THAN), and joined with AND, OR and NOT.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. CHECK.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 BALANCE PIC 9(4) VALUE 250.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    IF BALANCE > 100
        DISPLAY "Plenty saved"
    ELSE
        DISPLAY "Save more"
    END-IF.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: EVALUATE picks one branch out of many. The first WHEN that matches runs, and WHEN OTHER catches everything else. THRU matches a range.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. GRADE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 SCORE PIC 9(3) VALUE 82.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    EVALUATE SCORE
        WHEN 90 THRU 100 DISPLAY "A"
        WHEN 80 THRU 89 DISPLAY "B"
        WHEN 70 THRU 79 DISPLAY "C"
        WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "Try again"
    END-EVALUATE.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: A level-88 item gives a name to some values of the field above it. The name then reads like a true-or-false question, and SET ... TO TRUE moves the matching value in. Real programs use these everywhere for status codes.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. STATUS.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 ACCOUNT-STATUS PIC X VALUE "O".
   88 ACCOUNT-OPEN VALUE "O".
   88 ACCOUNT-CLOSED VALUE "C".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    IF ACCOUNT-OPEN
        DISPLAY "Open"
    END-IF.
    SET ACCOUNT-CLOSED TO TRUE.
    DISPLAY ACCOUNT-STATUS.
    STOP RUN.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(2) VALUE 10.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    IF N > 10
        DISPLAY "big"
    ELSE
        DISPLAY "small"
    END-IF.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: 10 is not greater than 10, so the ELSE branch runs.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 DAY-NO PIC 9 VALUE 6.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    EVALUATE DAY-NO
        WHEN 1 THRU 5 DISPLAY "Weekday"
        WHEN 6 WHEN 7 DISPLAY "Weekend"
        WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "No such day"
    END-EVALUATE.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: Two WHENs in a row share one action, so 6 or 7 prints Weekend. Only the first matching branch runs.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q3.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 LIGHT PIC X VALUE "G".
   88 STOP-NOW VALUE "R".
   88 GO-ON VALUE "G".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    IF STOP-NOW
        DISPLAY "Stop"
    ELSE
        DISPLAY "Go"
    END-IF.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: STOP-NOW is true only when LIGHT holds R. It holds G, so the ELSE branch runs.
Modern COBOL closes IF with END-IF. Older code ended the whole IF with a full stop instead, which made nested IFs easy to get wrong.

lessons.title: Loops and paragraphs
lessons.summary: PERFORM TIMES, UNTIL and VARYING, and named paragraphs.

sections.p: Loops are written with PERFORM. An inline PERFORM ... END-PERFORM repeats the statements inside it. TIMES gives a fixed count, and VARYING ... FROM ... BY ... UNTIL is a counting loop.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. COUNT.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 I PIC 9(2).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    PERFORM 2 TIMES
        DISPLAY "Hop"
    END-PERFORM.
    PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 3
        DISPLAY "Step " I
    END-PERFORM.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: PERFORM UNTIL tests the condition before each pass, so the body might not run at all. It stops as soon as the condition is true.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. DOUBLE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9(3) VALUE 1.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    PERFORM UNTIL N > 20
        DISPLAY N
        MULTIPLY 2 BY N
    END-PERFORM.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: A paragraph is a named block of statements, a little like a procedure with no parameters. PERFORM NAME runs it and comes back. Put STOP RUN before the paragraphs, or the program falls into them after the main part.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PARAS.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN-PARA.
    PERFORM GREET.
    PERFORM GREET 2 TIMES.
    STOP RUN.
GREET.
    DISPLAY "Hello from GREET".
sections.out:
Hello from GREET
Hello from GREET
Hello from GREET

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 I PIC 9.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    PERFORM VARYING I FROM 2 BY 2 UNTIL I > 6
        DISPLAY I
    END-PERFORM.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: I takes 2, 4 and 6. When it reaches 8 the UNTIL test is true and the loop stops before printing.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9 VALUE 5.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    PERFORM UNTIL N > 3
        DISPLAY "inside"
    END-PERFORM.
    DISPLAY "done".
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: N is already greater than 3, and PERFORM UNTIL checks before the first pass, so the body never runs.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q3.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN-PARA.
    DISPLAY "A".
    PERFORM SAY-B.
    DISPLAY "C".
    STOP RUN.
SAY-B.
    DISPLAY "B".
practice.why: PERFORM SAY-B jumps to the paragraph, runs it, and comes back to the next statement.

practice.q: What happens if you leave out STOP RUN before the paragraphs?
options: The program carries on into the paragraphs below
It loops forever from the top
practice.answer: The program carries on into the paragraphs below
practice.why: Statements run top to bottom, so without STOP RUN the paragraphs run once more after the main part.

sections.p: Data is described as records. A group item at level 01 holds smaller fields at higher levels such as 05. You can work with one field, or with the whole record as a single string of characters. This is how COBOL lays out each line of a bank file.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. RECORD.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 CUSTOMER.
   05 CUST-ID PIC 9(4) VALUE 17.
   05 CUST-NAME PIC X(6) VALUE "Hazel".
   05 CUST-NUTS PIC 9(3) VALUE 120.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY CUST-NAME.
    DISPLAY CUSTOMER.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: OCCURS repeats a field to make a table (an array). Subscripts are written in brackets and start at 1, not 0.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. TABLE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 STASH.
   05 NUTS PIC 9(2) OCCURS 3 TIMES.
01 I PIC 9.
01 TOTAL PIC 9(3) VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE 12 TO NUTS(1).
    MOVE 30 TO NUTS(2).
    MOVE 5 TO NUTS(3).
    PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 3
        ADD NUTS(I) TO TOTAL
    END-PERFORM.
    DISPLAY "Total " TOTAL.
    DISPLAY "Second " NUTS(2).
    STOP RUN.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 DATE-REC.
   05 YYYY PIC 9(4) VALUE 1959.
   05 MM PIC 9(2) VALUE 5.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    DISPLAY DATE-REC.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: A group item is all its fields side by side. MM is two digits wide, so 5 shows as 05.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 T.
   05 W PIC X(3) OCCURS 3 TIMES.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE "OAK" TO W(1).
    MOVE "ELM" TO W(2).
    MOVE "ASH" TO W(3).
    DISPLAY W(1).
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: COBOL subscripts start at 1, so W(1) is the first entry.

options: A loop that runs ten times
practice.why: OCCURS repeats the field to make an array. PERFORM is what loops.

practice.q: What is the first subscript of a COBOL table?
practice.why: COBOL counts table entries from 1.

lessons.title: STRING, UNSTRING and INSPECT
lessons.summary: Joining fields, splitting lines and counting characters.

sections.p: STRING ... INTO builds one field from several pieces. DELIMITED BY SPACE stops at the first space (so trailing padding is skipped); DELIMITED BY SIZE takes the whole sending item. The destination is not cleared first unless you MOVE SPACES into it yourself.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. STRJOIN.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 FIRST-NAME PIC X(8) VALUE "Hazel".
01 LAST-NAME PIC X(8) VALUE "Oak".
01 FULL-NAME PIC X(16).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    STRING FIRST-NAME DELIMITED BY SPACE
           " " DELIMITED BY SIZE
           LAST-NAME DELIMITED BY SPACE
           INTO FULL-NAME.
    DISPLAY "[" FULL-NAME "]".
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: UNSTRING splits a line on a delimiter into several fields. It is the usual way to pull apart a CSV-style record held in working storage.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. UNSTR.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 LINE-IN PIC X(24) VALUE "acorn,walnut,pecan".
01 N1 PIC X(8).
01 N2 PIC X(8).
01 N3 PIC X(8).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    UNSTRING LINE-IN DELIMITED BY ","
        INTO N1 N2 N3.
    DISPLAY N1.
    DISPLAY N2.
    DISPLAY N3.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: INSPECT ... TALLYING counts characters or runs of characters. INSPECT ... REPLACING rewrites them in place. Both are common on status codes and fixed-width records.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. INSP.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 MSG PIC X(12) VALUE "aaabaa".
01 N PIC 9(2) VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    INSPECT MSG TALLYING N FOR ALL "a".
    DISPLAY "count " N.
    INSPECT MSG REPLACING ALL "a" BY "x".
    DISPLAY MSG.
    STOP RUN.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 A PIC X(6) VALUE "Oak".
01 B PIC X(6) VALUE "Tree".
01 C PIC X(12).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    STRING A DELIMITED BY SPACE
           B DELIMITED BY SPACE
           INTO C.
    DISPLAY C.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: DELIMITED BY SPACE drops the padding on each field, and nothing puts a space between them.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q2.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 S PIC X(8) VALUE "abacab".
01 N PIC 9 VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    INSPECT S TALLYING N FOR ALL "a".
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: There are three a characters in abacab.

practice.q: What does DELIMITED BY SIZE mean on a STRING sender?
options: Take the whole field, including trailing spaces
Cut the field to one character
practice.answer: Take the whole field, including trailing spaces
practice.why: SIZE means the full picture width. SPACE stops at the first space.

options: Splitting one field into several on a delimiter
practice.answer: Splitting one field into several on a delimiter
practice.why: STRING joins; UNSTRING splits.

lessons.title: Sequential files
lessons.summary: SELECT, FD, OPEN, WRITE, READ and CLOSE.

sections.p: Real COBOL work is mostly files of records. SELECT in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION names a file and how it is organised. LINE SEQUENTIAL is a plain text file, one record per line — fine for learning and for many reports. The FD in the FILE SECTION describes each record. OPEN OUTPUT creates or replaces; WRITE adds a record; OPEN INPUT and READ walk the file; CLOSE finishes.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. NUTFILE.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT NUT-FILE ASSIGN TO "nuts.dat"
        ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD NUT-FILE.
01 NUT-REC PIC X(16).
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 DONE PIC X VALUE "N".
   88 FINISHED VALUE "Y".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    OPEN OUTPUT NUT-FILE.
    MOVE "acorn 12" TO NUT-REC.
    WRITE NUT-REC.
    MOVE "walnut 5" TO NUT-REC.
    WRITE NUT-REC.
    CLOSE NUT-FILE.
    OPEN INPUT NUT-FILE.
    PERFORM UNTIL FINISHED
        READ NUT-FILE
            AT END SET FINISHED TO TRUE
            NOT AT END DISPLAY NUT-REC
        END-READ
    END-PERFORM.
    CLOSE NUT-FILE.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: A READ needs an AT END path (or an equivalent status check). The usual pattern is a level-88 flag, set when the read hits the end, and a PERFORM UNTIL that stops on that flag. Forgetting AT END is a classic beginner bug.

practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT F ASSIGN TO "t.dat"
        ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD F.
01 REC PIC X(8).
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 DONE PIC X VALUE "N".
   88 FINISHED VALUE "Y".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    OPEN OUTPUT F.
    MOVE "one" TO REC.
    WRITE REC.
    MOVE "two" TO REC.
    WRITE REC.
    CLOSE F.
    OPEN INPUT F.
    PERFORM UNTIL FINISHED
        READ F
            AT END SET FINISHED TO TRUE
            NOT AT END DISPLAY REC
        END-READ
    END-PERFORM.
    CLOSE F.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: Records are written in order and read back the same way.

practice.q: What does ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL mean?
options: A text file with one record per line
practice.answer: A text file with one record per line
practice.why: LINE SEQUENTIAL maps each WRITE to a line of text. Mainframe shops often use plain SEQUENTIAL with fixed-length records instead.

practice.q: Where do you declare SELECT and ASSIGN?
practice.why: SELECT links the COBOL file name to an external path before the FD describes the record.

options: An AT END path (or status check)
practice.answer: An AT END path (or status check)
practice.why: Without AT END, hitting the end of the file is undefined behaviour in many compilers.

sections.p: A table can be searched with SEARCH when it has an INDEXED BY index name. SET index TO 1 starts at the first entry. SEARCH walks forward until a WHEN condition matches, or AT END if nothing does. This is the COBOL way to look up a code in a small in-memory table.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. SRCH.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 STASH.
   05 NUT-ROW OCCURS 4 TIMES INDEXED BY NIX.
      10 N-NAME PIC X(8).
      10 N-QTY PIC 9(3).
01 WANT PIC X(8).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE "acorn" TO N-NAME(1)
    MOVE 12 TO N-QTY(1)
    MOVE "walnut" TO N-NAME(2)
    MOVE 5 TO N-QTY(2)
    MOVE "hazel" TO N-NAME(3)
    MOVE 9 TO N-QTY(3)
    MOVE "pecan" TO N-NAME(4)
    MOVE 2 TO N-QTY(4)
    MOVE "hazel" TO WANT
    SET NIX TO 1
    SEARCH NUT-ROW
        AT END DISPLAY "missing"
        WHEN N-NAME(NIX) = WANT
            DISPLAY "found " N-QTY(NIX)
    END-SEARCH.
    MOVE "oak" TO WANT
    SET NIX TO 1
    SEARCH NUT-ROW
        AT END DISPLAY "missing"
        WHEN N-NAME(NIX) = WANT
            DISPLAY "found " N-QTY(NIX)
    END-SEARCH.
    STOP RUN.

sections.p: For a large table that is kept sorted, SEARCH ALL does a binary search. The table needs a KEY IS clause and the data must already be in key order. Day-to-day code often uses plain SEARCH on small tables and file lookups for big ones.

   05 R OCCURS 3 TIMES INDEXED BY IX.

practice.q: What must you do before SEARCH?
options: SET the index to the starting entry (often 1)
practice.answer: SET the index to the starting entry (often 1)
practice.why: SEARCH continues from the current index. Starting at 1 scans the whole table.

practice.q: What does INDEXED BY name on OCCURS declare?
practice.why: The index is not a PIC 9 field; SET and SEARCH manage it.

lessons.title: Project: a nut-crew payroll
lessons.summary: Tables, EVALUATE, edited money and a full-time bonus.

sections.p: A tiny payroll for three squirrels: each has a name, an hourly rate and hours worked. Gross pay is rate times hours. Anyone on 8.0 hours or more is full-time and gets a 10% bonus; the others are part-time with no bonus. The program prints each name, the final amount and an F/P status, then the crew total — the same shape as a payslip summary from a batch job.
sections.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. NUTPAY.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 CREW-SIZE PIC 9 VALUE 3.
01 CREW.
   05 WORKER OCCURS 3 TIMES.
      10 W-NAME PIC X(8).
      10 W-RATE PIC 9(2)V99.
      10 W-HOURS PIC 9(2)V9.
      10 W-GROSS PIC 9(4)V99.
01 I PIC 9.
01 TOTAL PIC 9(5)V99 VALUE 0.
01 MONEY-OUT PIC ZZZ9.99.
01 NAME-OUT PIC X(8).
01 BONUS PIC 9(3)V99.
01 STATUS-CODE PIC X.
   88 FULL-TIME VALUE "F".
   88 PART-TIME VALUE "P".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    MOVE "Hazel" TO W-NAME(1)
    MOVE 12.50 TO W-RATE(1)
    MOVE 8.0 TO W-HOURS(1)
    MOVE "Pip" TO W-NAME(2)
    MOVE 10.00 TO W-RATE(2)
    MOVE 6.5 TO W-HOURS(2)
    MOVE "Rowan" TO W-NAME(3)
    MOVE 11.25 TO W-RATE(3)
    MOVE 7.0 TO W-HOURS(3)
    PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > CREW-SIZE
        MULTIPLY W-RATE(I) BY W-HOURS(I) GIVING W-GROSS(I)
        EVALUATE TRUE
            WHEN W-HOURS(I) >= 8.0
                SET FULL-TIME TO TRUE
                COMPUTE BONUS = W-GROSS(I) * 0.10
            WHEN OTHER
                SET PART-TIME TO TRUE
                MOVE 0 TO BONUS
        END-EVALUATE
        ADD BONUS TO W-GROSS(I)
        ADD W-GROSS(I) TO TOTAL
        MOVE W-NAME(I) TO NAME-OUT
        MOVE W-GROSS(I) TO MONEY-OUT
        DISPLAY NAME-OUT MONEY-OUT " " STATUS-CODE
    END-PERFORM.
    MOVE TOTAL TO MONEY-OUT
    DISPLAY "TOTAL   " MONEY-OUT
    STOP RUN.
sections.out:
Hazel    110.00 F
Pip       65.00 P
Rowan     78.75 P
TOTAL    253.75

sections.p: Write each payslip line with STRING, save the report to a LINE SEQUENTIAL file, or look up a tax rate from a small table with SEARCH.

practice.q: Why does Hazel print 110.00 instead of 100.00?
options: An 8.0-hour day gets a 10% bonus on top of rate × hours
practice.answer: An 8.0-hour day gets a 10% bonus on top of rate × hours

practice.q: What does EVALUATE TRUE buy you here?
options: A clear multi-way branch on conditions, not on one variable
practice.answer: A clear multi-way branch on conditions, not on one variable
practice.why: EVALUATE TRUE with WHEN conditions is COBOL's structured way to choose among rules.

practice.q: What status letter does Pip get?
practice.code:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. Q1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 HOURS PIC 9(2)V9 VALUE 6.5.
01 STATUS-CODE PIC X.
   88 FULL-TIME VALUE "F".
   88 PART-TIME VALUE "P".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    EVALUATE TRUE
        WHEN HOURS >= 8.0 SET FULL-TIME TO TRUE
        WHEN OTHER SET PART-TIME TO TRUE
    END-EVALUATE.
    DISPLAY STATUS-CODE.
    STOP RUN.
practice.why: 6.5 is below 8.0, so the OTHER branch sets PART-TIME.
